title: Generative AI for learning: Investigating the potential of synthetic learning videos
venue: Proceedings of the International Conference of Artificial Intelligence in Education 2023
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether AI-generated synthetic instructional videos can support learning as effectively as traditionally produced instructor videos in an online micro-learning context. The authors focus on a practical educational question: whether generative AI can be used to create viable learning media that preserve learning outcomes and learner experience while reducing production time and cost.

The intervention was a synthetic learning video created with Synthesia, featuring a photorealistic AI-generated instructor matched to the original human instructor. The control condition used the same instructional content presented in a traditional instructor-produced video. Both versions were embedded in otherwise identical micro-learning courses delivered on the EdApp mobile learning platform, including a pre-test, a 4.5-minute instructional video, an activity, and a post-test. Adult learners from a global professional learning community were randomly assigned to the two conditions (n = 83).

Results showed that participants improved significantly from pre- to post-learning in both conditions, but there were no statistically significant differences in knowledge gains between the AI-generated and traditional video groups. Learner perception measures also showed no significant differences between conditions. The authors conclude that AI-generated synthetic instructional videos may be a viable substitute for traditional instructional videos in online education, though the study is limited by its small sample, brief assessments, and immediate post-test design.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a randomized controlled comparison with pre/post assessment and a non-AI baseline, which is stronger than correlational evidence. However, it is a small single-study trial with brief assessments and limited power, so it falls short of blue-tier evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The main learning outcome showed no meaningful difference between conditions, and the only notable between-group difference was a non-significant medium effect on one perception item. Overall impact is unclear and modest at best because the study suggests equivalence rather than a positive advantage over baseline.

interventions.use_case: mobile-delivered micro-learning course with an AI-generated synthetic instructor video versus a traditional instructor video
generative AI text-to-video synthetic learning video using a realistic AI-generated virtual instructor created with Synthesia

finding.finding_summary: In a randomized comparison with adult learners (n=83), the AI-generated synthetic video condition did not significantly differ from the traditional instructor video condition on learning gains. Knowledge gains were similar for the experimental group (M gains=1.00, SD=1.04, n=52) and control group (M gains=0.94, SD=1.13, n=31), with regression showing no condition effect (β=.03, p=.80, r=.03) and no effect after controlling for prior knowledge (β=-.03, p=.79).
finding.measure: pre-post knowledge assessment scores; difference scores (post minus pre)
finding.std_deviation: Experimental SD=1.04; Control SD=1.13; Full sample SD=1.11

finding.finding_summary: Learner experience ratings did not differ significantly between the AI-generated synthetic video and traditional video conditions on four Likert-scale items (all p>.46). The paper reports identical response patterns for three items and a medium-sized but non-significant difference for 'video met my expectations' (Cramer's V=.27), suggesting no reliable difference in perceived experience at the current sample size.
finding.effect_size: V=.05 to .27 depending on item; strongest noted V=.27
